soul.hero_subtitle: History, languages and stories: discover Benin through those who keep it alive.

heritage.title: Heritage retold
heritage.intro: Every site has a story that unfolds over time.

abomey.intro: Capital of the former Kingdom of Dahomey, Abomey preserves the royal palaces, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
abomey.source: Presentation text, to be validated with the Historical Museum of Abomey and UNESCO.

events.title: Birth of the kingdom
events.text: The Kingdom of Dahomey grows around Abomey. Successive kings build their palaces there.

events.title: The kingdom at its height
events.text: Under kings Ghézo and Glèlè, the kingdom is an organised regional power with an army and an administration.

events.title: War against France
events.text: King Béhanzin resists French troops, then is exiled in 1894. The kingdom comes under colonial rule.

events.title: World Heritage
events.text: The royal palaces of Abomey are inscribed on UNESCO's World Heritage List.

ouidah.intro: A historic port on the Gulf of Benin, Ouidah is both a place of memory of the slave trade and a major centre of Vodoun.
ouidah.source: Presentation text, to be validated with local institutions and the UNESCO Slave Route project.

events.title: A major slave-trade port
events.text: Ouidah becomes one of the main embarkation points of the Atlantic slave trade on the coast.

events.title: The Portuguese fort
events.text: The Portuguese build the São João Baptista de Ajudá fort, now a history museum.

events.title: Ouidah 92
events.text: The Ouidah 92 festival highlights Vodoun and the memory of the Slave Route.

events.title: National Vodoun Day
events.text: 10 January becomes a public holiday celebrating Benin's indigenous religions.

portonovo.intro: Official capital of Benin, Porto-Novo blends African, Brazilian and colonial heritage, with many museums.
portonovo.source: Presentation text, to be validated with the museums of Porto-Novo.

events.title: A coastal kingdom
events.text: A kingdom develops around the lagoon and trade with the coast.

events.title: The French protectorate
events.text: The town comes under French protectorate, then becomes an administrative centre of the colony.

events.title: The nation's capital
events.text: Porto-Novo remains Benin's official capital, while Cotonou concentrates economic activity.

events.title: Museums and architecture
events.text: Royal palace, museums, a Brazilian-style mosque: the town is best explored on foot, museum by museum.

languages.title: Explorer of Beninese languages
languages.empty_text: These phrases will be completed and validated with native speakers.

stories.title: Cultural stories
respect: Ask permission before photographing a ceremony.
Some places and rites are reserved for initiates.
Go with a trusted local guide.
A ceremony is not a show.

chapters.title: The origins
chapters.text: The Kingdom of Dahomey is born around Abomey and is organised around its kings.

chapters.title: The palaces
chapters.text: Each king builds his own palace: together they form a UNESCO-listed site today.

cards.title: The Slave Route
cards.summary: A path of memory in Ouidah.

chapters.title: The path
chapters.text: In Ouidah, a path of about four kilometres links the town to the beach.

chapters.title: The Door of No Return
chapters.text: A monument facing the ocean honours the people who were deported.

chapters.title: Weaving and basketry
chapters.text: These techniques are passed down within families, from workshop to workshop.

chapters.title: Bronze
chapters.text: Bronze casting is an ancient art still practised by craftspeople.

chapters.title: The deities
chapters.text: Vodoun honours deities linked to nature and ancestors.

chapters.title: Visiting with respect
chapters.text: This text is provisional and must be validated with initiates before publication.
